## Seth Moulton is a father, a husband, a Marine, and a Democrat with a mission to bring a new generation of leaders to Congress.
Join Team Moulton.
## Serve America
Serve America is transforming Congress by supporting a new generation of leaders who put people over politics.

pages.title: Priorities — Seth Moulton for Congress
pages.text:
## Keeping Our Country Safe and Secure
In the Marines, our division’s motto was “no better friend, no worse enemy.” That means your allies trust you, and your enemies trust your resolve. Our country should be no different. But the Trump administration turned its back on our friends and cozied up to our adversaries. His erratic foreign policy weakened the country, left our allies in the lurch, and emboldened our adversaries across the globe. That needs to change.
When it comes to national security, our solution has too often been only “more:” more ships, more troops, more spending. But instead of always fighting with more, we have to fight smarter. No more building outdated, costly weapons systems—we need to make sure our troops have the best technology to defeat our adversaries and support our allies. That means dramatically increasing our investment in autonomous, hypersonic, and cyber weapons—and continuing to invest in basic scientific research, education, and immigration.
But to restore strong American leadership, we need to use all the tools at our disposal—from foreign aid to new alliances to diplomacy—not just the military. We should build new alliances, like a Pacific NATO, to counter the growing threats of Russia and China abroad. And we need to take care of those who take care of us, whether it’s an ally in the Paris Climate Accord or the veterans who fight our wars.
Our troops deserve it and our national security demands it.
## Preventing Gun Violence
As a United States Marine, I carried an assault rifle in Iraq. It saved my life more than once. I’ve seen what assault rifles can do. Nobody in America needs to own an assault rifle. I also carried two grenades every day I was in Iraq, but we’ve made a decision in this country that our citizens don’t need to walk around carrying hand grenades. We need to do the same thing with assault weapons and other weapons of war. Nobody is allowed to drive a tank down the highway, or walk into a shopping mall with grenades—nobody should be allowed to have an assault weapon either.
It’s time for commonsense gun reform. We can start by passing an assault weapons ban and background checks, not letting people who are on a terrorist no fly list buy guns, and enforcing red flag laws.
## Ensuring Health Care—and Mental Health Care—For All
Healthcare is a basic human right, not a privilege. All Americans deserve health insurance that’s affordable, that isn’t tied to a job, and that covers all pre-existing conditions—no matter who you are.
That’s why I support President Obama’s original plan to make private health insurance work better, alongside a public option. Competition is the cornerstone to Americans getting lower premiums, lower drug prices, and great care. We need to undertake drastic change to fix our healthcare system, and we need to give Americans the freedom to choose the plan that works best for them.
In addition, mental health should become a routine part of healthcare in our country. We all know someone who struggles with mental health or struggle with it ourselves. But all too often, we don’t talk about these issues or get help because of the stigma associated with them. That’s why I passed a bill to make 988 the national mental health crisis hotline.
It’s time to end the stigma around these issues and make sure everyone gets the support they need.
## Creating an Economy that Works for Everyone
Our economy is changing fast, and we need to equip Americans with the tools they need to thrive in the new economy—not the old. That means investing in infrastructure, reimagining our education system, and rewriting the rules of our economy to build an America where hard work pays off.
We need to pass a Democratic Tax Reform that ensures everyone pays their fair share. That means at least :
Reversing the Trump tax cuts and raising the rates for corporations and top earners.
Taxing capital gains at the same rate as working Americans.
Funding the IRS so that tax shelters and tax cheats are audited, not ordinary Americans.
We also need to create equal opportunity in this country by closing school funding gaps, so that the quality of education does not depend on your zip code, improving workforce development programs to put more Americans in good paying jobs, and making college affordable to revive the American Dream that has been out of reach for so many.
## Supporting our Veterans
Our veterans sacrifice so much to take care of us overseas, so it’s our responsibility to ensure they are taken care of when they return home.
Veterans are at high risk of facing mental health challenges: 50% of veterans who struggle with post-traumatic stress (PTS) don’t get help, and 22 veterans or active-duty service members commit suicide every day.
My plan to make mental health check-ups as routine as a physical for active-duty military and veterans would:
Require annual mental health check-ups just like annual physicals. Mindfulness training is preventative medicine as pioneered today by the special operations community and other elite units.
In addition, require a mandatory counseling session for everyone returning from a combat deployment within two weeks of arriving home.
Fill all mental health vacancies at the VA and adopt a more holistic approach to treatment, including alternative therapies like mindfulness, exercise, and cannabis. Fund an ad campaign for veterans’ families to recognize mental health symptoms.
## Reforming our Immigration System
We need a path to citizenship for everyone in America. I’m proud to have cosponsored and voted for HR 6, the Dream and Promise Act, which would create a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers who are American in every way except on paper. It should be law.
We shouldn’t be cutting off foreign aid or closing the border or building a wall. We should be investing targeted foreign aid in the Northern Triangle, addressing the violence that’s driving people from their homes and to our borders.
When the president separated families and put kids in cages I was speaking out and fighting back. I led a delegation to the Mexican side of the border and met with deported veterans—a phrase that shouldn’t even exist.
## Championing Equality for All Americans
There is systemic racism in our country, and one of the most important things I’ve learned over the last few months is how prevalent it is right here at home. That’s a difficult lesson to learn.
We’re still feeling the repercussions of the past, and we need to address them. We need to have a conversation in this country that should have happened decades ago. I am a co-sponsor of HR40, which would create a commission to examine reparations. I’ve also introduced the GI Bill Restoration Act, which seeks to right historical wrongs by extending housing and education GI benefits to certain direct descendants of Black WWII veterans, who were denied them.
I also believe we need to rethink the way we police in this country. We should be diverting funds from police departments to social services; from policing crime to preventing crime; for providing more mental health support to people in our communities before they get caught up in the criminal justice system.
We’re facing two primary challenges in this country right now. The first is that our economy is changing faster than ever before, and Americans everywhere are being left behind. The second is climate change. That’s why we need a Green New Deal: because if we do it right, we can solve both problems at once.
The Green New Deal needs to be built around green jobs and clean energy, decarbonization and breakthrough technologies, and access to green energy for the developing world—and America should lead the way in winning this moral and economic opportunity. We can lead the world in green tech and green jobs, and we should set the standards for other countries to follow.
The New Deal paved the way for a strong economy and American leadership in the last century. Let’s shape the Green New Deal to help America lead this one.
## Building Infrastructure of the Future
We can rebuild our economy by rebuilding our country. That starts with connecting every house in America to affordable, high-speed internet. And it means not just repairing our roads, bridges, and water pipes but building next-generation transportation, like high-speed rail, because everyone should have access to good jobs in their region and a chance to make it home after work in time for dinner.

## A New Generation of Leadership.
Seth is a fighting for the people of the North Shore and is working to bring a new generation of leaders to Washington.
Thank you for joining Team Moulton!
Since taking office in 2015, Congressman Seth Moulton and his team have been hard at work making a difference for the constituents of Massachusetts’ 6th congressional district and people across the country. We’re proud of all the work we’ve done and look forward to tackling the challenges that lie ahead.
Congressman Moulton’s priorities include advocating for quality and accessible mental health care, combating climate change, ending the scourge of gun violence, bolstering public transportation, and ensuring the national security of our country. Congressman Moulton’s political organization, Serve America, supports service-oriented candidates running for federal office. All are impressive and inspiring leaders.
If you’re interested in volunteer opportunities with Seth’s re-election campaign or if you would like to get in touch with Seth Moulton's political team in MA-06 or Serve America, please call (617) 209-9816.
Congressman Seth Moulton saw the consequences of failed leadership in Washington first-hand over the course of his four tours as a Marine in Iraq. In 2017 he founded Serve America to help elect a new generation of service–driven leaders from military, national security, and public service backgrounds who are willing to put the country first and take on the tough challenges in Washington.
Learn About Serve America

pages.title: The American Affordability Agenda | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## The American Affordability Agenda
There are two Americas today – one for the wealthy and well-connected, and one for everyone else. In an economy where President Trump’s policies have made his billionaire friends even wealthier, tens of thousands of Massachusetts families are struggling to make rent, are about to lose their health care coverage, and are having to turn down their thermostats to save cash. That’s wrong, and it’s un-American.
That’s why I have proposed an “ American Affordability Agenda” to level the playing field and provide every American with a strong foundation for achieving the American Dream. My plan is based on the principle that housing, healthcare and education are human rights. We have an obligation to ensure that every American has affordable housing and energy, quality healthcare, and a modern education that stretches from pre-school to the workforce. These “3 for 30” are my counter to the MAGA Project 2025 and will provide working families with a concrete Democratic plan for a more affordable future. I know it’s not enough for Democrats to just oppose Trump – we need to stand for and deliver a positive vision forward for all Americans. Republicans are squandering our future – it’s time for Democrats to do the patriotic thing and lead.
We will pay for the policies that will make housing, healthcare and education human rights for all Americans through a national wealth tax on mega-millionaires and by closing tax loopholes that favor corporations, the wealthy and the well-connected . By putting the excessive wealth of the top 0.1% to work and refusing to use the tax code to reward hoarders of wealth, we can raise over $3.5T over the next ten years to ensure that those who work hard in this country can once again achieve the American Dream.
## Housing is a Human Right
- Ban private equity firms from scooping up homes and driving up real estate costs
- Help homebuyers by providing additional mortgage assistance
- Protect renters by strengthening the ability to negotiate rents
- Protections for food assistance so families aren’t forced to choose between paying rent and putting food on the table.
Long-Term Cost Reduction
- Build the homes Massachusetts needs by lowering the barriers to infill housing
- Create more affordable housing by investing in high-speed and regional rail and building more ADU’s
- Lower energy costs by increasing clean energy production (including next-generation nuclear), removing the barriers put in place by the Trump administration, and undertaking permitting reform
## Healthcare is a Human Right
- Lower prescription drug costs by extending annual cap on out-of-pocket expenses on drugs to all insurance plans
- Protect reproductive healthcare by codifying Roe v. Wade protections into federal law
- Expand access to maternal care by increasing federal funding for services
- Lower healthcare premiums by extending the enhanced ACA subsidies
Long-Term Cost Reduction
- Make healthcare more accessible by eliminating pharmacy deserts
- Create competition for private insurers through a national public option to lower premiums
- Lower drug costs by restricting the role that Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBM’s) play
## Education is a Human Right
- Provide universal pre-k with a federal guarantee of a seat for every 4-year-old
- Expand workforce training by expanding free community college and vocational options
- End predatory student lending by holding financial institutions accountable
Long-Term Cost Reduction
- Reform the US Department of Education from just K-12 to support pre-k through workforce training
- Provide training that meets the moment by investing enough in vocational schools to meet rising demand, and prepare our kids for AI and other innovative technologies

pages.title: Know Your Rights: Immigration/ICE | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## Know Your Rights: Immigration/ICE
This is not Rep. Moulton’s official Congressional/Government website – this is his campaign website. If your intention was to visit his official House of Representatives website, please click here.
## Know Your Rights
Ask for a warrant: ICE needs a valid warrant signed by a judge to enter your home or search your belongings. You do not have to open the door until you see one. If they are in your home without a warrant, you can ask them to leave and tell them that you do not consent to a search of your home.
You have the right to remain silent: You may refuse to speak to law enforcement officers, including immigration officers. You may also say that you want to remain silent.
You are not required to share any personal information such as your place of birth, immigration status or criminal history when asked, but you cannot lie or share any false documentation.
Do not show or use any false or fraudulent documentation , including a fake name.
You have the right to speak to a lawyer: You do not have to sign anything or hand officials any documents without first speaking to an attorney.
Before you sign anything, talk to a lawyer. ICE may try to get you to sign away your right to see a lawyer or a judge. Be sure you understand what a document actually says before signing it.
Inform the ICE officer if you have children . If you are the parent or primary caregiver of a U.S. citizen or permanent resident who is under age 18, ICE may “exercise discretion” and let you go.
Report and document raids and arrests . Document or record the encounter or raid details and involved officer names or numbers to share with attorney and advocacy organizations.
## Make a Plan for ICE Encounters
In the event that you encounter immigration officials, make a plan with your family or household in advance and create an emergency caretaking plan for any dependents.
Always carry with you a copy of any valid immigration document you have . Make sure to store the originals in a safe place and ensure your family knows where they are and have access to them. Do not carry papers from another country with you, such as a foreign passport. Such papers could be used against you in the deportation process.
Write down and memorize emergency contact information , such as that of your family members or a lawyer, and ensure everyone within your household does the same.
Memorize your immigration number (A-Number or Alien Registration Number) and share it with your family. If you are detained, this will help your loved ones find you.
Familiarize yourself with local officials and keep a signed ICE Privacy Waiver , which will authorize any officials to advocate on your behalf without putting you at risk.
Ask for a bond hearing before an immigration judge , If you are denied release after being arrested for an immigration violation.
## If You Believe Your Rights Were Violated
Write down everything you remember and document injuries , including badge numbers and patrol car numbers, what agency the officers were from and contact information for witnesses. If you’re injured, seek medical attention immediately and document your injuries.
File a written complaint with the agency’s internal affairs division or civilian complaint board.
Additionally, you can report it here: https://www.mass.gov/forms/report-misconduct-by-federal-agents
## Free or Inexpensive Legal Resources
MIRA Immigration Helpline – The helpline provides general information and resources on immigration processes, rights, and what to do after detention, but does not offer individual legal advice or representation. Schedule consultation: https://calendly.com/miralegalhelpline or call (508) 293-1817
Lawyers for Civil Rights’ Immigrant Defense Hotline – Receive free, same-day legal advice on questions about enforcement actions like raids or deportations by staff and pro bono attorneys here: (617) 988-0606
Local Sixth District Resources
Northeast Justice Center – The Northeast Justice Center helps low-income and elderly residents of Northeast Massachusetts obtain justice and empowerment through skillful, creative, and persistent advocacy both for systemic change and with high-quality individual representation. Address: 181 Union Street, Suite 201B, Lynn, MA 01901, Phone: (978) 458-1465
Northeast Justice Center’s “Immigration Hotline” – Receive telephonic immigration consultation, information, and referrals for income-eligible immigrants from Essex County and Northern Middlesex County here: (781) 599-7730 or here (toll-free): (888) 657-2889
New American Center – Provides services to new arrivals and refugees including ESL classes, employment support, case management, health education, tutoring, youth programs, cultural activities, housing mediation, and more. Address: 330 Lynnway, Suite 302, Lynn, MA 01901 Phone Number: (781) 593-0100
Lynn Rapid Response Network – Offers support to immigrant communities by providing legal information about immigrant rights & socal social services in the North Shore. Contact form : https://www.lynnrapidresponse.org/contact
## Resources for International Students
Specifically view this section, found in the ‘Know Your Rights’ section of the resource hub: Travel Emergency Preparedness Plan for Individuals Traveling within the U.S. (March 2025)
This is a template that goes into detail about what documents to have available in case of a travel emergency, personal information to share with a trusted contact, and other considerations. Travel Emergency Preparedness Plan
American Immigration Lawyer’s Association (AILA) lawyer search website: https://ailalawyer.com/ . You can search by area of expertise, in this case: “Students and Exchange Visitors.”
For anyone who is specifically concerned about their situation, perhaps they attended a protest or published an opinion piece that might put a target on their back from this Administration, you may consider consulting with an attorney to discuss those concerns. Unfortunately, we are living in a different reality than 3 months ago. People need to be prepared.
## Available in Additional Languages:
You can search for more using the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) referral search here: www.ailalawyer.com .
## Online self-service tools:
- Attorney General Hotline – Report bias-motivated harassment and threats here: 1 (800) 994-3228
- Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) – Find information related to immigration court cases. This is an automated line where users need to input A#: 1 (800) 898-7180
- Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE) – Online Detainee Locator System (ODLS) Individuals looking for loved ones that may have been detained can search for the location of detainees by entering A# and country of birth on the following website: https://locator.ice.gov
- Northeast Justice Center’s “Immigration Hotline” – Receive telephonic immigration consultation, information, and referrals for income-eligible immigrants from Essex County and Northern Middlesex County here: (781) 599-7730 or here (toll-free): (888) 657-2889
- MIRA Immigration Helpline – The helpline provides general information and resources on immigration processes, rights, and what to do after detention, but does not offer individual legal advice or representation. Schedule consultation: https://calendly.com/miralegalhelpline or call (508) 293-1817

pages.title: Protecting Election Integrity | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## Protecting Election Integrity
Given the threats from the Trump administration to nationalize or influence elections, Democrats need to prepare today to protect the integrity of our democratic process. My Election Integrity Agenda lays out a plan to protect our electoral process and ensure that the will of the people – not the will of the White House – determines our political leaders.
Prohibit federal agents at polling places
- Federal agents and the military have no place at polling locations. Voters should never be intimidated while casting their personal vote, nor should they be scared to go to the polls for fear of intimidation, harassment, or violence from agents of their own government.
Prohibit using federal funds to “take over” or “nationalize” elections
- America has a long, democratic history of empowering states to oversee their own elections, and Donald Trump’s threats to “nationalize” elections should concern anyone who cares about the integrity of our democratic process. I will work in Congress to ensure that no federal funds are used to support any effort by Trump or his administration to manipulate elections.
Recruit and train poll workers and election monitors
- Our poll workers and election monitors bravely protect the integrity of our elections. We must prepare them for the kinds of threats, intimidation, and misbehavior they may see if the President attempts to undermine voters at the ballot box.
Legal protections against intimidation and harassment of election officials and poll watchers
- If we want to safeguard the integrity of our elections, we have to start by protecting the individuals that make the election process possible. To ensure that election officials and poll watchers feel safe when performing their duty, there must be serious legal ramifications for those who attempt to intimidate, harass, or in any way pressure election workers.
Increase funding to update outdated infrastructure and cybersecurity
- Outdated voting machines and unprotected software risk the trustworthiness of our elections and undermine public trust in this important process. Federal funding must be directed toward updating election infrastructure and strengthening cybersecurity to guarantee that when Americans cast their ballots, they have complete confidence in the systems that receive their vote.
Commit Trump officials, GOP office holders, and Military and Civilian authorities to a peaceful transfer of power .
- We should not rely on hope or norms when democracy is being tested. Congress must use its oversight role and other constitutional powers to demand clear public commitments from administration officials, military leaders, and elected officials to respect the results of elections and support a peaceful, orderly transition of power. It is time to stop being reactive and demand more in advance.
Clarify that federal law cannot compel states to hand over private election information absent clear congressional authorization.
- No American should be fearful that by performing their civic duty, they risk their information being handed over to an administration that is vilifying its opponents and trying to suppress their vote. Federal law is clear: states cannot be compelled to give up the private information of their citizens without congressional approval. Your vote and your data is your own. We must stand firmly by the law to keep it that way.
I pledge to do all I can to ensure the 2026 elections remain free and fair. But all of us can contribute to that end. Here is what you can do to help defend the 2026 elections:
Work the Polls
Poll workers are the unsung heroes of our elections, and the job is getting harder. Sign up through your local elections office to work for our democracy.
Watch the Polls
Partisan and nonpartisan poll watchers observe elections to ensure fairness. Volunteer with your local party committee or nonpartisan group to do so.
Support Protecting Elections
You can help by supporting nonpartisan organizations that defend election workers and the election process. Donate to the Campaign Legal Center, Carter Center’s democracy program, Election Official Legal Defense Network.

pages.title: Prediction Markets | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## Prediction Markets
When government officials possess material, non-public information about when and where the next bomb will fall, and then use that knowledge to make hundreds of millions of dollars on offshore markets, they’re insider trading on the blood of our troops. They have a financial incentive to see the conflict escalate and a personal interest in keeping the American people in the dark.
We need to shut down the “Death Markets” once and for all. We need to ban federal officials from trading on the outcomes they control or insider knowledge of, prosecute offshore rule-breakers, and investigate the conflicts of interest between this administration and the companies facilitating these bets.
In my office, the rule is already in effect: we don’t bet on the mission. It’s time we forced the rest of Washington to follow suit.
Commitment to Not Participate
- I imposed a policy spanning both my Congressional and campaign teams stating that neither I nor anyone on my teams would use prediction markets to bet on government actions or outcomes nor profit from any information learned as a result of the job.
Ban Death Markets
- Ban prediction markets pertaining to war, terrorism, assassination, or death
Strengthen and Enforce Insider Trading Protections
- Provide the CFTC with the explicit legal authority to combat and prosecute illicit insider trading within prediction markets.
- Ban federal elected officials, political appointees, Executive Branch employees, and congressional staff from trading prediction market contracts tied to government policy, government action, or political outcomes when they possess material nonpublic information.
Uphold US Law and Prosecute Rulebreakers
- Crack down on the offshore prediction markets offering illegal bets on war while encouraging insider trading.
- Push federal commodities regulators to change their hands off-approach and instead police market manipulation, prosecute all rulebreakers, and ensure US government employees comply with existing laws.
Prosecute Government Lawbreakers and War Profiteers
- Investigate and contest conflicts of interest between the Trump administration, Trump family members, and the leading prediction markets companies.

pages.title: Equality for Every American | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## Equality for Every American
No one should be treated as less than equal in the country they call home. Yet too often, politicians on the right use hatred and bigotry to divide us, targeting people based on who they love, how they identify, or where they come from. That politics of cruelty has no place in Massachusetts or in America.
This is a frightening moment for many in the LGBTQ+ community — especially transgender Americans who are being singled out and attacked for political gain. Let me be clear: your identity is real. Your presence is vital. Your humanity is non-negotiable. No one should have to live in fear for simply being who they are.
We cannot stand by while politicians attempt to erase, intimidate, or strip rights from LGBTQ+ Americans. In the Senate, I will continue to fight to pass full federal LGBTQ+ anti-discrimination policies to ensure that no American has to hide who they are to keep a job, rent an apartment, access healthcare, or serve their country.
- Finally pass The Equality Act — long overdue legislation that would make clear, nationwide, that discrimination has no place here.
- Healthcare is a Human Right . Efforts to deny gender-affirming care or restrict medically necessary treatment are dangerous and cruel. To those seeking care and being blocked by politics: I will work to protect your access to care and ensure that decisions about healthcare are made by patients and doctors — not politicians.
- Mental Healthcare Saves Lives — and It Must Be Protected. LGBTQ+ youth, especially transgender youth, face higher rates of bullying, depression, and suicide risk. I led the creation of the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, which has already connected millions of Americans to lifesaving support, and I am working to restore and protect specialized services for LGBTQ+ youth within 988, because no young person in crisis should lose help due to politics. Mental healthcare is healthcare — and I will fight to ensure every person can access it when they need it most.
- Ensure Protections for Every American , regardless of race, sexual preference, or gender identity. I was a cosponsor of the Transgender Bill of Rights when it was first introduced last Congress, in 2023, and am proud to cosponsor it again in 2026. I have also fought for years to ensure our transgender troops can serve openly and proudly. Anyone willing to put on the uniform and defend this country deserves respect.
Democrats must do more than defend against attacks. We must lead, and build a country where every person — regardless of race, sexual orientation, or gender identity — can live openly, safely, and with dignity.
Equality for all is not optional. It is who we are supposed to be. And it is a promise worth fighting for.

pages.title: Mental Health & Placing Our Kids' Well-Being Before Big Tech's Profits | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## Mental Health & Placing Our Kids’ Well-Being Before Big Tech’s Profits
Mental health touches every community. Whether you live in a red state or blue state, a city or small town: everybody in America knows somebody who has suffered from mental illness, and parents can see that our nation’s young people are facing a mental health crisis.
This is personal for me. After serving in Iraq, I experienced post traumatic stress, and I have been open about how hard it can be to speak up and get help. That is why I have fought so hard in Congress to reduce the stigma around mental health and to improve access to quality care. I led the effort to create the national 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, which provides lifesaving assistance to any American.
- Expand Access to Care : People suffering from mental illness and addiction should be able to access care, including telehealth and long-term in-patient treatment. We must also address the chronic underfunding of programs that help keep people off the streets.
- Countywide Crisis Intervention Centers : Build on proven pilot projects that have already demonstrated success in Massachusetts.
- Nationwide Ban on Cell Phones in Schools : Condition federal funding on local education agencies establishing and enforcing reasonable restrictions on cell phone use during classroom instructional time.
- Mental Health Screenings in Schools : Provide the resources that will enable schools to provide regular, free mental health screenings for students
- Social Resiliency Trust Fund : Tax social media companies and use those funds to build more public spaces and invest in youth organizations that encourage social connection. Provide safe public spaces that tie communities together.

pages.title: Putting Working Families First | Seth Moulton for Massachusetts
pages.text:
## Putting Working Families First
Massachusetts has some of the highest childcare costs in the country. Parents have enough on their plates without being squeezed by the skyrocketing cost of raising children while also caring for aging grandparents.
- Increased Funding for Childcare : We should be expanding the childcare workforce, paying childcare workers more, and building new childcarecenters. Parking lot attendants often get paid more to watch cars than childcare workers get paid to take care of our children. We should also make it possible to co-locate childcare and senior care facilities.
- Support for Full-year Head Start : Every child deserves the opportunity for success, and yet about 20% of Head Start staff positions nationwide were recently vacant due to low pay. I have fought to secure millions in federal funding for Lynn’s Head Start campus—creating 15 new classrooms and space for hundreds of children in a model of year-round early education that strengthens families.
- Expanded Child Tax Credit : The CTC cuts child poverty and provides peace of mind to parents. We should make permanent the improved child tax credit that was passed during the pandemic despite repeated Republican efforts to cut it.
- Expanded Vocational Ed: Cover GED and trade school feesand greatly expand apprenticeship programs.The skills needed for careers that last a lifetime will change over time. A lifetime of learning must not only be accessible but rewarding. Pell Grants also need to help young people cover the actual cost of getting an education today.
- Support Job and Manufacturing Training : I helped bring together GE, labor, and educators to launch a nearly $8 million investment in Lynn’s E-Team machinist training initiative. Together, we can build an expanded pipeline for high-skill, high-wage jobs in advanced manufacturing and deliver lasting results in job placement, wage growth, and opportunity for working families.
